title: AI Unlocked: The Humanities
blurb: For writers, historians, linguists, artists, and scholars: research and archival workflows, translation and close-reading at scale, creative collaboration without losing your voice, and the authorship debates every humanist must be able to argue.

modules.d: Why the humanities are central — not peripheral — to the AI era.
modules.body:
The claim

AI is trained on the human record; its biases, beauty, and blind spots are humanities questions. Humanists who master the tools become indispensable interpreters of the age — and gain research leverage their predecessors could not imagine.

  • What LLMs actually are, told honestly: prediction over the archive of human text.
  • The distant-reading tradition meets its most powerful instrument.
Jaron Lanier’s warning (You Are Not a Gadget) — that technology quietly redefines personhood unless humanists intervene — is this course’s founding premise. UNESCO’s ethics framework leans on exactly the concepts humanists steward: dignity, culture, meaning. The archive needs its interpreters fluent in the machine.

modules.d: Sources, OCR, chronology-building, and honest citation.
modules.body:
Workflows

  • OCR + AI cleanup of scanned archives; structured extraction into chronologies and entity lists.
  • Literature mapping with Elicit/Consensus; long-context interrogation of entire monographs (NotebookLM/AI Studio).
  • Citation integrity: AI-invented references are endemic — verify every source; disclose AI assistance per your journal/press.
plAIbox™: process one small archive (letters, articles, records) into a queryable knowledge base and publish three findings with verified citations.
🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

You are my research assistant for a humanities project on [topic]. Build a research plan: key primary sources and where they live, five essential secondary works, a chronology skeleton, two competing interpretive frames I must engage, and a list of every factual claim you made that I need to verify independently.

Workflows

  • Working translations with register options — then your philological judgment pass.
  • Close-reading partner: "Identify every image pattern in this poem; argue two competing interpretations; cite lines."
  • Low-resource languages: capabilities and gaps — and how scholars are building corpora (an opening for African-language work Team21 cares about deeply).

modules.t: Creative Collaboration Without Losing Your Voice
modules.d: Drafting, world-building, and the iterative craft loop.
modules.body:
The craft loop

  • AI as sparring partner: outlines, alternatives, critiques — the sentences that matter remain yours.
  • Voice preservation: feed your corpus as style reference; reject homogenization consciously.
  • World-building engines for fiction; constraint-based poetry exercises; the Team21 authoring process (from Level 1) at literary depth.

modules.d: Copyright, training-data ethics, and how to argue about them well.
modules.body:
The debates every humanist should command

  • Authorship: what disclosure norms publishers and prizes now require.
  • Training-data ethics and the live litigation landscape (positions, not verdicts).
  • Cultural homogenization vs democratized creation — steelman both.
  • Your own position paper, defended in seminar.

modules.t: Capstone: A Work of AI-Assisted Scholarship or Art
modules.d: The artifact plus the honest process memoir.
modules.body:
Capstone

  • One substantial artifact (paper, translation, creative work, or digital archive) with a full process disclosure: where AI contributed, where you overruled it, and what that taught you about the craft — presented to the panel.
